question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ -14 & -16 & -2\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & a & ∗ \\ 0 & b & ∗ \\ -2 & c & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $2a+c.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the Jordan matrix $J$ may be written as a composition of Jordan blocks, as follows:

$$
J={J}_{2}(5)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(-2)
$$

So, we have

- a single $2\times 2$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =5,$ and

- a single $1\times 1$ block corresponding to $\lambda =-2.$

Therefore, the columns of $P$ form the following chains: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{2}(5) & : & {v}_{2}\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }0 &  \\ {J}_{1}(-2) & : & {v}_{3}\overset{A+2I\,}{\to }0 & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =5,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}$ such that $(A-5I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}.$

Now, computing $A-5I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ -14 & -16 & -2\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -14 & -16 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A-5I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -14 & -16 & -7 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-14 & -16 & -7 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have ${x}_{2}=1.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-14{x}_{1}-16\cdot 1-7{x}_{3}=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}-1.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}-1 \\ 1 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=0,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $2a+c=2\cdot (-1)+0=-2.$
